title: Bounded runtime of the circuit encoder
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean input and output symbols, and let $C,d,n$ be natural numbers. There is a time $t \le 60(k+1)(L+30)(C+4)^3(n+1)^{3(d+1)}$, where $k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$ and $L$ is the maximum length of the instruction templates in the counter program constructed from $M$, such that this program, started with all eleven registers equal to zero, at its initial label, and with empty output, halts after $t$ steps on the word $1^n0\,1^{(C+1)(n+1)^d}0$ and has output equal to the encoding of the circuit at input length $n$ in the family constructed from $M,C,d$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Boolean symbols
The counter program is run on the specified input word
The initial state has the designated initial label, all eleven registers zero, and empty output
The time is bounded by $60(k+1)(L+30)(C+4)^3(n+1)^{3(d+1)}$, with $k$ the number of work tapes and $L$ the maximum template length
The program halts and outputs the encoded circuit specified by the constructed family at input length $n$
